rulesApplied.benchmarkAuditRetentionRule: A benchmark audit can survive only if a public two-week replay can change method ordering or a scientific conclusion; field-only checks, generic leakage checkers, and known split hygiene are rejected.
rulesApplied.defectClaimRule: No defect claim is allowed without an inspected public sample or metadata path, an applicable checkpoint, and forward reachability. Static code observations are recorded only as contract evidence.
rulesApplied.primarySourceRule: Method, dataset, benchmark, and asset facts are supported only by formal papers, official project pages, official repositories, official dataset documentation, or fixed code artifacts.
rulesApplied.independentUnitRule: Frames, overlapping windows, targets from one physical event, and repeated ego projections are not presumed independent.

candidateLedger.title: Replace Co-MTP future truth with receiver-available proposals
candidateLedger.formalEstimand: For the same forecasting case and fixed model family, the paired change in trajectory risk from replacing post-t0 ego and other-agent truth with proposals generated only from information available by t0.
candidateLedger.independentUnit: Physical forecasting scene or non-overlapping source sequence, not agents or frames within one scene.
candidateLedger.successCondition: A public, non-oracle forward path runs and changes a method conclusion beyond repository repair.
candidateLedger.killCondition: No compatible public sample, checkpoint and forward path, or the result is only that oracle input outperforms a feasible proposal.
candidateLedger.evidenceStatus: Static oracle-future flow verified; sample, checkpoint and forward closure absent.

candidateLedger.title: Causal per-arrival cooperative forecasting instead of one-shot full-history consumption
candidateLedger.formalEstimand: The paired risk difference between a state updated only by messages received by each decision time and a one-shot model given the completed observation window, under the same final payload set.
candidateLedger.successCondition: A fixed public checkpoint yields a reproducible method-order change under causal arrival replay and the gap is not explained by observation length alone.
candidateLedger.killCondition: No compatible checkpoint and message-timing sample, or the candidate duplicates the previously blocked prefix-causality asset family.
candidateLedger.evidenceStatus: Direct streaming neighbors exist; the cooperative prefix-replay asset remains blocked and no forward was reached.

candidateLedger.title: Cross-agent identity association using only receiver-observable evidence
candidateLedger.formalEstimand: The paired forecasting or tracking loss when cross-agent association is computed from receiver-visible geometry, timing and appearance versus a pipeline that may use dataset-global identity for routing, target selection or preprocessing.
candidateLedger.independentUnit: Physical sequence with identity permutation applied consistently within each sender stream.
candidateLedger.successCondition: A field reaches the test-time forward or pre-association path, an identity-preserving intervention changes outputs, and the effect survives evaluator-invariance controls.
candidateLedger.killCondition: IDs only select benchmark targets or score outputs, no checkpoint forward is reachable, or the work duplicates the active pseudonym/anonymous handoff family.
candidateLedger.evidenceStatus: IDs are present and used in preprocessing and target lookup; raw global identity as a learned deployment feature was not established.

candidateLedger.title: Forecasting effect of annotated pre-associated tracks versus online detector-tracker histories
candidateLedger.formalEstimand: The paired cooperative gain over ego-only when a frozen predictor consumes annotated histories, official pre-fused histories, or histories produced online by a fixed detector and tracker.
candidateLedger.independentUnit: Source sequence, with all target views and windows from one sequence kept together.
strongBaselines: CoopTrack or another learned association pipeline
candidateLedger.successCondition: The input intervention changes the ordering of at least two methods on the same sequence ledger and is reproducible from public checkpoints.
candidateLedger.killCondition: The benchmark is explicitly an annotated-trajectory task, no compatible detector-tracker-predictor checkpoints exist, or the result is only generic perception-to-prediction degradation.
candidateLedger.evidenceStatus: Task input is clearly trajectory-based; no end-to-end public forward chain was assembled.

candidateLedger.title: Method ordering under Online-VIC histories versus Offline-VIC infrastructure predictions
candidateLedger.formalEstimand: The interaction between method identity and infrastructure-information regime for paired forecasting risk on the same scenes.
candidateLedger.independentUnit: Forecasting scene grouped by source sequence and intersection.
candidateLedger.successCondition: Public checkpoints and the same scene ledger reproduce a method-order change that alters the paper-level conclusion about cooperative forecasting.
candidateLedger.killCondition: Only aggregate published rows are available, checkpoint bytes cannot be loaded, or the comparison simply restates the benchmark's existing Online/Offline split.
candidateLedger.evidenceStatus: The comparison is already explicit in V2X-Seq; linked checkpoints were not loaded and no new intervention remains.

candidateLedger.title: RSU and map-location memorization as a method-order intervention
candidateLedger.formalEstimand: The method-by-location-regime interaction comparing official splits with held-out physical locations while preserving observable scene and target distributions.
candidateLedger.independentUnit: Intersection or fixed RSU deployment, not frames or short scenes.
candidateLedger.successCondition: A public two-week replay changes method ordering after location is the independent unit and the effect survives distribution matching and coordinate-equivariance controls.
candidateLedger.killCondition: Only split fields or a probe are produced, full metadata and checkpoints are unavailable, or the output is standard train-test split hygiene.
candidateLedger.evidenceStatus: Location fields and fixed infrastructure are documented; no ranking intervention was executed.

candidateLedger.title: Recompute forecasting conclusions at the physical-event rather than sliding-window unit
candidateLedger.formalEstimand: The paired method-risk contrast averaged over independent physical events, compared with the contrast averaged over released windows or targets.
candidateLedger.independentUnit: Continuous source event reconstructed from time, location and trajectory overlap.
candidateLedger.successCondition: At least two fixed methods reverse order or a published uncertainty conclusion changes under a replayable event ledger.
candidateLedger.killCondition: No public full manifest and per-case outputs, the event grouping is chosen after outcomes, or the output is only wider confidence intervals.
candidateLedger.evidenceStatus: Window and track schemas are documented; no complete physical-event ledger or fixed multi-method output was available.

candidateLedger.title: Same-checkpoint open-loop gain to closed-loop harm sign reversal
candidateLedger.formalEstimand: For each route and fixed planner, the paired cooperative-minus-ego-only effect on open-loop perception or forecasting risk and on closed-loop driving utility using the same detector checkpoint.
candidateLedger.independentUnit: Closed-loop route or physical scenario, clustered across repeated seeds if any.
candidateLedger.successCondition: A bounded public replay produces route-level sign reversals that change detector ordering and are stable across fixed planner controls.
candidateLedger.killCondition: MDrive already directly covers the conclusion, checkpoint bytes are not verified, CARLA setup exceeds the replay window, or only different model families are compared.
candidateLedger.evidenceStatus: A valid code intervention and scenario sample exist, but MDrive directly states the gap and no local closed-loop route ran.

candidateLedger.title: Veto cooperative evidence by downstream planner value
candidateLedger.formalEstimand: The paired closed-loop utility of accepting versus withholding one cooperative evidence set, conditional only on receiver-visible state before planner execution.
candidateLedger.independentUnit: Route-level decision episode, with repeated decisions nested within route.
candidateLedger.successCondition: The policy uses only pre-decision observables and outperforms direct planning-conditioned selectors in a public closed-loop replay.
candidateLedger.killCondition: The mechanism reduces to a score threshold, conformal selector, query/fuse/ego fallback, or another name for directly covered planning-conditioned fusion.
candidateLedger.evidenceStatus: Direct mechanisms and the sequence-level harm-calibration closure preempt the proposed selector family.

candidateLedger.title: Rank cooperative forecasters on a t0-defined target cohort with explicit censoring
candidateLedger.formalEstimand: Expected forecasting loss over targets eligible from receiver-observable information at t0, with exit, death, missed detection and unscored status represented explicitly rather than dropping unavailable futures.
candidateLedger.independentUnit: Physical scene; target-level terms are nested within scene.
candidateLedger.successCondition: A public case ledger shows a reproducible method-order change caused by outcome-dependent target inclusion and the t0 cohort resolves it without post-t0 fields.
candidateLedger.killCondition: Target inclusion is fixed by the benchmark, no per-case missingness ledger exists, or the work is only mature missing-data estimation applied to one benchmark.
candidateLedger.evidenceStatus: Masks and scoring categories exist, but outcome-dependent cooperative target censoring and a ranking consequence were not demonstrated.

candidateLedger.title: Joint existence and trajectory prediction for disappearing cooperative targets
candidateLedger.formalEstimand: Joint proper risk for target existence and trajectory conditional on existence, evaluated on a t0-defined receiver-observable cohort.
candidateLedger.independentUnit: Physical scene or sequence, with targets nested within it.
candidateLedger.successCondition: The joint model changes planner-relevant decisions or method ordering on natural target disappearance events with public data and checkpoint execution.
candidateLedger.killCondition: Only synthetic masks are available, no natural event labels or forward path exist, or the method is a direct transfer of established imputation and variable-history models.
candidateLedger.evidenceStatus: Adjacent methods cover incomplete histories; natural cooperative disappearance events and an executable planner consequence are unverified.

candidateLedger.title: Compare methods on receiver-observability-matched target sets
candidateLedger.formalEstimand: Cooperative-minus-ego-only performance within target strata defined only by what the receiver can observe before fusion.
candidateLedger.independentUnit: Physical scene or route; visibility-stratified targets remain nested.
candidateLedger.successCondition: The strata change method ordering and predict an intervention not already implemented by receiver-aware selection methods.
candidateLedger.killCondition: The result reproduces the directly published visible/invisible split or remains a label-only benchmark audit.
candidateLedger.evidenceStatus: The exact visibility-conditioned negative-transfer problem is directly covered.

candidateLedger.title: Test whether each newly arrived cooperative history can reduce forecast or plan value
candidateLedger.formalEstimand: For a fixed receiver state and arrival order, the incremental change in prediction risk and downstream plan utility after admitting the next causally available message.
candidateLedger.independentUnit: Message-arrival episode grouped by physical route or trajectory scene.
candidateLedger.successCondition: Natural message arrivals yield reproducible non-monotonic method ordering and a receiver-observable intervention not reducible to an existing selector.
candidateLedger.killCondition: Only synthetic packet order is available, no message-level checkpoint replay exists, or the result is another generic admission threshold.
candidateLedger.evidenceStatus: No natural cooperative forecasting arrival trace plus compatible checkpoint was verified.

candidateLedger.title: Shadow benchmark fields against a receiver-observable deployment schema
candidateLedger.formalEstimand: Difference in model outputs after removing fields absent from the receiver contract while holding raw observations and model state fixed.
candidateLedger.successCondition: A field reaches a fixed public forward path and its removal changes method ordering or a scientific conclusion.
candidateLedger.killCondition: The result is field inspection, a generic leakage checker, static schema mismatch, or cannot reach a checkpoint forward.
candidateLedger.evidenceStatus: Field differences were observed statically; the user-specified direct-reject rule applies.

reasons: No compatible public sample, checkpoint and forward path was established.
A trivial oracle-to-feasible gap would not by itself create a new scientific conclusion.
The prefix-causality asset family was already blocked in v9.
No cooperative message-timing sample and fixed checkpoint forward were verified.
Global IDs were not proven to enter a learned test-time feature rather than preprocessing or target selection.
It collides with the active pseudonym/anonymous handoff family and lacks forward evidence.
V2X-Seq explicitly defines a trajectory-input forecasting task.
No public end-to-end detector-tracker-predictor checkpoint chain was assembled.
Online and Offline regimes are already explicit benchmark rows.
Checkpoint links were observed but no checkpoint bytes or forward results were verified.
Only location fields and fixed infrastructure were verified.
Without a two-week multi-method order change this is known split hygiene and is directly excluded.
No complete physical-event ledger and fixed per-case multi-method outputs were available.
Uncertainty correction without changed ordering or conclusion is audit-only.
MDrive directly states the open-loop to closed-loop gap and exposes the paired intervention path.
CARLA and checkpoint execution were not completed in the audited environment.
Select2Drive and Defer to Plan directly cover planning-relevant selection and fusion.
The remaining veto is a generic selector already closed by the harm-calibration audit.
Outcome-dependent cooperative target inclusion and an actual ranking consequence were not demonstrated.
Without that evidence the contribution is benchmark estimation using mature missing-data tools.
Natural cooperative target disappearance labels and planner consequences were not verified.
The architecture would otherwise be a transfer of established imputation and variable-history forecasting.
The visible/invisible negative-transfer split is directly covered by Selective Language Communication.
The residue is a label and benchmark audit.
No natural message-arrival trace and compatible forecasting or planning checkpoint were verified.
A thresholded admission rule would duplicate existing selectors.
No field removal reached a fixed checkpoint forward and changed ordering.
Static field checks and generic leakage checkers are directly excluded.

conclusion.summary: The search found credible contract risks and several already documented evaluation gaps, but no candidate simultaneously had a distinct unclosed mechanism, receiver-observable inputs, an applicable public sample or metadata path, a compatible checkpoint, forward reachability, a two-week replay, and an outcome capable of changing method ordering or a scientific conclusion.
decisiveBoundaries: Co-MTP future truth is a verified static input-flow concern, but public reproduction is blocked and no oracle-gap claim is allowed.
V2XScenes has a verified current-release configuration mismatch, but data-level overlap, checkpoint provenance and ranking effects are unproved; generic split hygiene is rejected.

V2X-Seq exposes IDs, masks, intersection fields, online/offline regimes and public loaders, but these do not establish receiver-oracle use, target censoring bias, map memorization, or causal prefix failure without compatible sample and forward evidence.
MDrive already covers open-loop to closed-loop non-monotonicity and provides a paired code path; recreating that benchmark result is not a new Idea, and the local closed-loop stack was not run.
